edits.old: that built and ran the 4,000 MW supercritical coal-fired Mundra Ultra Mega Power Project in Gujarat.
edits.new: that built and ran the supercritical coal-fired Mundra Ultra Mega Power Project in Gujarat. The plant's two capacity figures are different quantities, and a regulator's order says which is which: the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission, in its order of 20 June 2025 on CGPL's own petition 168/MP/2019, gives the installed capacity as 4,150 MW (five units of 830 MW) and the net plant capacity as 4,000 MW (five units of 800 MW) after the motor-driven boiler feed pump, adding that the net capacity remains 4,000 MW despite each unit being rated 830 MW. The 4,000 MW figure is the basis of the power purchase agreement, and is the one the IFC's disclosure uses.
